_scope_note: F2/F3 (evidence/audit2/Cascade.md:254-296): the final-sweep text must count as turn output, and the route budget must cover warmup/StartCascade/Send/retry/polling/detach instead of starting at the poll loop. Both defects were reproduced at 2598299e (streamed 'answer' -> 502 EMPTY_RESPONSE; 100 ms budget -> 310 ms behind a 250 ms Send) and re-pinned here against the fixed producer. The expectCaught:false entry records the measured equivalent survivor and the premise behind it.
_baseline_provenance: Measured 2026-11-19 on Windows, Node v24.19.0, base eecd3819 plus the Cascade JWT cancellation change. Four JWT lifecycle tests increase the combined suite from 19 to 23. Command: node --import ./test/setup-env.mjs --test test/cascade-final-sweep-terminal.test.js test/cascade-turn-deadline.test.js. Result: 23 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The Send RPC now takes its preframed body. Its mutation still removes the remaining-time bound from that same call. Historical full sweep: 6 caught and 2 expected survivors at 19/19 on the 2026-10-26 baseline, recorded in evidence/final/DeadlineFlake.md.

mutations.name: F2: the idle_empty classifier arm ignores delivered output again — a turn whose text arrived in the final sweep is reported as an empty upstream failure (502 EMPTY_RESPONSE) after the bytes were streamed

SURVIVOR (equivalent while both sweep arms mark sawText): the terminal reason drops the `|| totalYielded > 0` half. No producer path can reach the clause any more, so only a future sweep arm that advances totalYielded without sawText would exercise it; the clause is kept as the audit-specified second layer behind the per-arm marking, and mutation 1 proves the classifier still refuses to turn delivered bytes into an empty failure
F2: the final sweep stops marking the turn as having text — a detached turn's snapshot freezes sawText=false, so the resume path resurrects the empty-turn verdict after delivering the answer

F3: the poll window is granted the full route budget again. With five milliseconds left after Send, the first poll wait must stop at the original deadline with a typed max_wait result and zero trajectory reads. The fake clock observes that terminal before any per-RPC timeout can mask the late wakeup
mutations.anchor: const maxWait = Math.max(0, turnStart + turnBudgetMs - startTime);

mutations.name: F3: a phase failure after the deadline is no longer converted to the route-budget stop — a Send/StartCascade that ran out of turn time surfaces as a transport error, which rotates accounts and retries a request that has no time left

F3: the last-tick deadline tolerance collapses to zero — a phase timer that fires on the deadline's final wall-clock millisecond rethrows `gRPC unary timeout`, the exact B06 CI flake (attempt 2: 120.24 ms StartCascade test)
F3: the Send RPC loses its remaining-time bound — a Send issued inside the budget can run to gRPC's 30 s default, so the turn returns after the deadline instead of stopping at it
F3: the shared workspace warmup is awaited without the deadline race — a warmup started by another request can hold a short route for the full multi-RPC handshake
